claimLedger.wording: Noah is the managed AI desktop-support product at onnoah.app.
claimLedger.excerpt: Noah is an AI desktop support app for Mac and Windows

claimLedger.wording: The managed Mac offer specifies macOS 12+, Apple Silicon and Intel.
Noah documents read-only diagnosis followed by explicit approval for destructive/system-modifying actions and an action log.
claimLedger.excerpt: Diagnostic actions (reading system state, listing processes, checking disk usage) are read-only and run automatically. Every action is logged inside the app.
claimLedger.scope: Do not imply every diagnostic needs a click, guaranteed safety or independent audit

claimLedger.wording: Diagnosis is advertised as always free; the entire first conversation includes fixes, without a card.
claimLedger.excerpt:
Find out what's actually wrong — always free, every time
Your whole first conversation, fixes included
claimLedger.scope: Managed offer; do not say unlimited free fixes

claimLedger.wording: Managed Noah advertises $8.99/month and Guardian $79/year; monthly explicitly covers up to three Mac or Windows computers and annual says the same all year.
claimLedger.excerpt:
NOAH MONTHLY
$8.99
a month

Something's broken and you want it sorted.

Everything Noah can fix — as often as you need
Up to 3 of your computers, Mac or Windows
claimLedger.additionalExcerpt:
NOAH GUARDIAN
$79
a year

You'd rather not think about it again.

The same, all year
claimLedger.scope: Dollar symbol only: currency code and taxes not established. Fair-use limits apply; amounts at checkout not tested. No unlimited guarantee.

claimLedger.wording: The advertised seven-day trial requires a card and new-customer eligibility; someone Noah has already fixed something for is charged on subscribing instead.
claimLedger.excerpt: If Noah has already fixed something for you, there is no trial to start and you are charged when you subscribe — checkout says which before you confirm.
claimLedger.scope: Recurring renewal until cancelled; no payment/trial attempted

claimLedger.wording: Managed Noah is proprietary; the related Noah for Tinkerers source is AGPL-3.0.
claimLedger.excerpt: The Noah desktop product is proprietary.
claimLedger.additionalExcerpt: Noah for Tinkerers is the open-source, bring-your-own-key build of Noah
claimLedger.scope: Edition-specific, not a licence conflict; do not call managed subscription AGPL

claimLedger.wording: Tinkerers documents a user-supplied Anthropic key, direct Claude requests, no account or subscription, and opt-out usage telemetry/update checks.
claimLedger.excerpt: You bring an Anthropic API key; Noah talks to Claude directly from your machine. No subscription and no account
claimLedger.additionalExcerpt: the only other network calls are an update check and an anonymous, opt-out usage ping
claimLedger.scope: Tinkerers only; AI-provider usage costs not priced here; not offline AI

claimLedger.wording: Managed Noah requires email before answering the first question; conversations go through api.onnoah.app to an AI provider and are kept as repair history.
claimLedger.excerpt: Your email address. Noah asks for it during setup and needs it before it will answer your first question.
claimLedger.additionalExcerpt: Your conversations and repair history — while we provide Noah to you, and for our continuing review of the quality of its answers. These are not deleted on a fixed schedule.
claimLedger.scope: Policy last updated September 12, 2026; no account or backend testing

claimLedger.wording: The privacy policy distinguishes file names/sizes from content, but says specific crash reports, system logs or settings files may be read and enter the conversation.
claimLedger.excerpt: Specific files, when a diagnosis needs one — a crash report, a system log, a settings file. Noah opens the named file, and what it reads becomes part of the conversation.
claimLedger.scope: Qualifies homepage 'never opens your files'; do not repeat blanket no-file-reading/no-data-leaves-device claims

workflow.title: A slow Mac with a full disk: choose the next diagnostic, not the next cleaner
workflow.primaryIntent: Decide whether a slow/full Mac needs symptom-led repair or a storage-owner and recurring-growth investigation.
workflow.distinctMechanism: Separate a low-free-space observation from CPU pressure, crashes and network symptoms; choose evidence and approval scope before deleting anything. Contrast managed Noah and Tinkerers only where edition matters.
workflow.leadDirection: A full disk and a slow Mac can coexist without identifying the same cause. Read-only inspection first; choose Noah for a broader software-symptom workflow or inspect storage ownership/history when that is the actual job. No unsupported causal threshold or speedup.
outline: Record symptom, free-space context and backup status without running cleanup
Separate process pressure from growing storage; high CPU alone is not a fault
Read Noah's proposed diagnostic/fix boundary and managed data policy
Use storage-owner/project context for a cache/rebuild decision rather than deleting by size
Choose a managed support workflow, BYOK tooling or Breathing Room's qualified preview
workflow.interactionHandoff: Non-destructive decision checklist: symptom type, existing backup, evidence of recurring growth, AI-provider/email willingness, and preview/Python tolerance. No filesystem access, deletion recommendation or calculated savings.
workflow.visualPlan: Verified product UI immediately after lead; labelled Breathing Room Space example later. Rights and edition gate must pass first.
internalLinks: counterpart workflow/comparison reciprocal link; verify actual routes at drafting
workflow.affiliation: Say Breathing Room, which we build, beside the single bounded recommendation.
doNotClaim: full disk proves cause of slowdown
Breathing Room fixes Wi-Fi or Windows

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs Noah: storage maintenance or symptom-led repair?
comparison.primaryIntent: Choose between overlapping Mac tools without equating broader support repair with storage/activity maintenance.
comparison.lengthDirection: Concise decision lead, sourced matrix, edition sidebar and caveats; link to workflow instead of expanding duplicate intent.
comparison.decision: Noah merits consideration for its documented broader software-support symptoms; Breathing Room, which we build, merits consideration for storage-owner/project context and maintenance history, with preview limitations disclosed. Tinkerers suits readers prepared to manage an Anthropic key and provider charges.
requiredCaveats: No Tinkerers shell/licence behaviour transferred to managed

noahAdvantages: Documented broader software-symptom workflow beyond storage, with repair-plan approval and logs (N03/N13).
Advertised macOS 12+ support versus Breathing Room's macOS 13+ preview requirement (N02/BR1).
Separate AGPL BYOK edition documented for people who want direct Anthropic usage without a Noah subscription/account (N07/N08); provider costs remain.
noahTradeoffs: Managed email requirement, backend/AI-provider requests and conversation retention without fixed deletion schedule (N09/N10).
Trial eligibility, card, renewal and fair-use conditions; dollar currency code not established (N05/N06).
Managed/BYOK differences require deliberate edition choice (N07/N14); generic privacy/command claims would mislead.
breathingRoomAdvantages: Source-documented storage owner/project context, grouped app/helper monitoring and sampled local history fit the narrower storage-investigation job (BR2); not proof Noah lacks them.
Free local inspection/manual features and separately advertised AI Care pricing (BR1/BR3); not a cost/performance winner claim.
breathingRoomTradeoffs: Non-notarized preview, Python 3.10+ and incomplete native/Intel validation (BR1/BR4).
Hosted AI requires authentication/internet and relevant data transfer; daily care requires the app running and exact approvals, with optional Ruff auto mode caveat (BR3).
No verified Windows, hardware-repair, general Wi-Fi-fix or complete uninstall parity.
